text: {"answerable": true, "answer": "Backpropagating through an MD simulation (direct reverse-mode AD or the adjoint method) pushes the gradient through the entire trajectory generation [W3168247670#003]. DiffTRe instead uses thermodynamic perturbation theory and reweighting to bypass differentiation through the simulation for time-independent observables [W3168247670#001]. It differentiates only through the potential energy computation of decorrelated states [W3168247670#011]. This avoids exploding gradients, since DiffTRe gradient magnitudes stay constant with simulation length while direct AD gradients grow exponentially [W3168247670#011]. It also gives about 2 orders of magnitude speed-up in gradient computation [W3168247670#001], with memory requirements comparable to the adjoint method [W3168247670#003]. Direct AD, by contrast, is typically intractable beyond about a hundred particles and a few hundred time steps [W3168247670#003]. Previously generated trajectories can also be re-used, which cuts wall-clock time per update [W3168247670#011]. The cost is that dynamical properties cannot be used as target observables, because the reweighting makes DiffTRe invariant to the sequence of states [W3168247670#019]."}
